key_insight: Among four WC-10Co-4Cr thermal spray routes, HVAF and HVOF produce the best overall balance of high hardness, low wear, and strong corrosion resistance, while APS performs worst.
engineering_relevance: The study gives a direct process-selection guide for wear- and corrosion-critical steel components, showing how spray method strongly controls coating performance.
method: WC-10Co-4Cr coatings were deposited on 304 stainless steel by APS, DS, HVOF, and HVAF.
Microstructure, hardness, tribological behavior, and electrochemical corrosion performance were compared across the four processes.
Wear tracks and corrosion metrics were used to identify dominant failure and protection mechanisms.
evidence_signal: Compared with 304 stainless steel, coatings showed much higher hardness and lower wear rate, with HVAF reaching 1162.2 HV, a wear rate of 1.10×10^-5 mm3/N·m, and the best corrosion metrics (Ecorr -0.37 VSCE, Icorr 1.75 μA/cm²).
watch_item: Performance ranking is process- and test-condition-dependent, so coating selection should still account for substrate, service environment, and deposition parameter optimization.
paper_title: Microstructure, Wear and Corrosion Resistances of Atmospheric Plasma, Detonation, High Velocity Oxy-fuel and High Velocity Air-fuel Sprayed WC-10Co-4Cr Cemented Carbide Coatings
